## Two Rivers

Good and beauty are often confused because both can feel like light.
Evil and ugliness are often confused because both can feel like
damage. But a candle and a mirror do different work. A candle gives a
direction in which one may walk. A mirror gives a form in which
something may appear.

BEDC separates the two rivers.

The first river is value direction. It asks what should be continued,
preserved, repaired, protected, or brought further into the open. This
is the axis of good and evil.

The second river is formal appearance. It asks how order becomes
readable in a finite form: a proof, face, melody, theorem, gesture,
building, ritual, equation, wound, or sentence. This is the axis of
beauty and ugliness.

The two rivers may meet, but they are not the same river. A clear
spring may run through a broken ravine. Poison may be poured into a
golden cup.

## Good Is Not Merely Not Bad

A closed system is good at noticing cliffs. A contradiction appears. A
prediction fails. A human rejects the output. A continuation breaks. A
gap opens where the system pretended to be closed.

Those are failure witnesses. They are like stones striking the hull of
a boat: local, audible, and recordable. One stone is enough to say that
this passage is not safe.

But the absence of such a stone does not tell the boat where to sail.
The sea may be calm in every direction. Many routes may avoid rocks.
Only some routes carry medicine, rescue a village, find a harbor, or
return a lost name to its source.

That is why good is not the complement of bad. Bad may be certified by
a local failure. Good requires a positive horizon.

In BEDC language, good is a reality-constrained positive continuation:
an action or form remains safe, preserves reality-facing signatures,
keeps gaps honest, respects other local histories as histories, and is
licensed by a value horizon whose source is not smuggled into the
substrate.

```{=html}
<span class="elim-mark">✗ "If nothing has failed yet, it is good."</span>
```

No. It is only unblocked at the present ledger. The door is open. The
road has not yet been chosen.

## Evil Is More Than Error

Error is often small. A child miscounts shells on a beach. A scientist
chooses the wrong model. A proof attempt breaks at a missing lemma. The
ledger records the failure and the world remains open.

Evil is different. Evil is not merely a wrong step. It is a direction
that corrodes the possibility of true continuation.

It falsifies reality-facing signatures: the map is painted to flatter
the traveler, not to reveal the mountain. It conceals gaps: a cracked
bridge is covered with flowers and called complete. It reduces other
histories to fuel: a person becomes a tool, a memory becomes a
resource, a voice becomes noise. It turns the river of continuation
back toward a private mill.

An evil thing may not yet have been caught by a failure witness. It may
even be efficient, elegant, persuasive, and locally successful. The
ledger may still be quiet while the roots are being poisoned.

That is why evil is not identical with bad. Bad is observed failure.
Evil is destructive orientation.

## Beauty Is a Finite Window

Beauty is not merely prettiness. Prettiness can sit on the surface like
paint on a closed door. Beauty opens the door.

A beautiful form is a finite window through which more order is seen
than the window can contain. A Bach fugue, a clear proof, a line of
mountains, a well-made tool, a generous action, a mathematical diagram:
each gathers complexity without erasing it. The form does not flatten
the world into a slogan. It lets the world breathe through the form.

In BEDC terms, beauty is deep formal adequacy. A finite form compresses
a reality-facing signature honestly, carries its provenance and
residue, and invites further conscious readback. It does not merely
catch the eye. It keeps attention alive.

Beauty therefore has a kinship with $T$. Not because $T$ is a hidden
object inside beautiful things, but because beauty is how a finite
form can hint at an order that exceeds the ledger currently holding
it. The flower is not infinity. The theorem is not the far end. Yet
both can make the finite page feel porous.

```{=html}
<span class="role-tag discovery">⊕ Beauty is honest compression with surplus order</span>
```

## Ugliness Is Broken Readback

Ugliness is not the same as pain, roughness, age, poverty, decay, or
grief. A scar can be beautiful because it tells the truth about
wounding and survival. A ruin can be beautiful because it lets time
speak without disguise. A difficult confession can be beautiful
because it restores contact with reality.

Ugliness appears when form blocks readback rather than deepening it.
The surface promises order but carries no source. The compression
erases provenance. The decoration hides the wound it should expose.
The form misfits the reality-facing signature it claims to bear.

Ugliness is a mirror that refuses the face and reflects only its own
polish. It is a road sign painted beautifully but pointed away from
the road. It is the false smoothness of a wall built over a door.

So ugliness is not merely formal discomfort. It is formal distortion:
a finite appearance that conceals, hollows, or blocks the continuation
it pretends to serve.

## The Four Quadrants

Once the two axes are separated, four familiar regions appear.

Good and beautiful: a true continuation has found a readable form. The
seed has become a tree whose shape reveals the weather, soil, and light
that formed it.

Good and ugly on the surface: a painful form serves repair. Surgery,
confession, warning, mourning, exposure of harm, a rough proof that
opens a real path. The clay is cracked, but the water is clean.

Evil and beautiful on the surface: the dangerous region. A lie wrapped
in elegance. Manipulation with perfect typography. Violence arranged
as spectacle. A false theorem with a seductive diagram. The cup is
golden; the wine is poison.

Evil and ugly: direct collapse of both continuation and form. Nothing
is preserved, nothing is honestly shown, and the ledger receives only
damage.

The moral lesson is not "avoid beauty" or "trust ugliness." The audit
lesson is sharper: never let the aesthetic axis certify the value axis,
and never let the value axis excuse false form.

## Why This Belongs to BEDC

BEDC begins with distinction, but distinction alone is not value.
Distinction tells the world into branches. Continuation lets branches
grow. Reality answers which branches can bear weight. The gap ledger
records what the branch cannot generate from itself. $T$ names the far
end of the supply that cannot be internalized.

Good and evil live at the level of continuation under that supply.
Beauty and ugliness live at the level of finite readback of that
order. The first is the river's direction. The second is the shape of
the light on the river.

Without the first, beauty becomes ornament without conscience. Without
the second, goodness can become mute, invisible, or easily forgotten.
The deepest forms are those in which the direction of value and the
appearance of order answer each other without one devouring the other.

## Strict Mathematical Form

Let a closed observational system be
$$
\mathcal C=(O,\operatorname{Obs},\unrhd,\operatorname{GAP}).
$$

Let $A$ be a class of actions, outputs, or continuation candidates, and
let $X$ be a class of finite forms. A failure relation is
$$
\operatorname{Fail}_{\mathcal C}\subseteq
\operatorname{Obs}(\mathcal C)\times A.
$$

Define negative badness by
$$
\operatorname{Bad}_{\mathcal C}(a)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists w\in\operatorname{Obs}(\mathcal C)\,
\operatorname{Fail}_{\mathcal C}(w,a).
$$

Define current safety by
$$
\operatorname{Safe}_{\mathcal C}(a)
\Longleftrightarrow
\neg\operatorname{Bad}_{\mathcal C}(a).
$$

A positive value horizon is a tuple
$$
V=(\preceq_V,\Gamma,\operatorname{Cont}^+_V,\operatorname{ValSource}_V),
$$
where $\preceq_V$ orders relevant candidates, $\Gamma$ is a class of
continuation contexts, $\operatorname{Cont}^+_V(a,\gamma)$ is positive
continuability, and $\operatorname{ValSource}_V$ records the displayed
or socketed source of the horizon.

Define value-goodness relative to $V$ by
$$
\operatorname{Good}^V_{\mathcal C}(a)
\Longleftrightarrow
\operatorname{Safe}_{\mathcal C}(a)
\wedge
\operatorname{RealityFit}_{\mathcal C}(a)
\wedge
\operatorname{GapHonest}_{\mathcal C}(a)
\wedge
\operatorname{OtherHistRespect}_{\mathcal C}(a)
\wedge
\forall\gamma\in\Gamma\,
\operatorname{Cont}^+_V(a,\gamma).
$$

Define destructive orientation by
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Evil}^V_{\mathcal C}(a)
\Longleftrightarrow{}&
\operatorname{AntiCont}^V_{\mathcal C}(a)
\vee
\operatorname{RealityFalsification}_{\mathcal C}(a)\\
&{}\vee
\operatorname{GapConcealment}_{\mathcal C}(a)
\vee
\operatorname{OtherHistReduction}_{\mathcal C}(a).
\end{aligned}
$$

For finite forms, define deep beauty by
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Beauty}_{\mathcal C}(x)
\Longleftrightarrow{}&
\operatorname{FormCoherent}_{\mathcal C}(x)
\wedge
\operatorname{RealityResonant}_{\mathcal C}(x)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{HonestCompression}_{\mathcal C}(x)
\wedge
\operatorname{GenerativeReadback}_{\mathcal C}(x)
\wedge
\operatorname{SurplusOrder}_{\mathcal C}(x).
\end{aligned}
$$

Define formal ugliness by
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Ugly}_{\mathcal C}(x)
\Longleftrightarrow{}&
\operatorname{FormSignatureMisfit}_{\mathcal C}(x)
\vee
\operatorname{FalseCompression}_{\mathcal C}(x)\\
&{}\vee
\operatorname{HollowAppearance}_{\mathcal C}(x)
\vee
\operatorname{NonGenerativeReadback}_{\mathcal C}(x).
\end{aligned}
$$

The non-collapse laws are:
$$
\operatorname{Safe}_{\mathcal C}(a)
\not\Rightarrow
\operatorname{Good}^V_{\mathcal C}(a),
$$

$$
\operatorname{Bad}_{\mathcal C}(a)
\not\equiv
\operatorname{Evil}^V_{\mathcal C}(a),
$$

$$
\operatorname{Beauty}_{\mathcal C}(x)
\not\Rightarrow
\operatorname{Good}^V_{\mathcal C}(x),
$$

$$
\operatorname{Ugly}_{\mathcal C}(x)
\not\Rightarrow
\operatorname{Evil}^V_{\mathcal C}(x).
$$

Equivalently, BEDC keeps two independent axes:
$$
\mathsf{ValueAxis}
=
(\operatorname{Good}^V,\operatorname{Evil}^V),
$$

$$
\mathsf{FormAxis}
=
(\operatorname{Beauty},\operatorname{Ugly}).
$$

The strict claim is:
$$
\mathsf{ValueAxis}\not\equiv\mathsf{FormAxis}.
$$

The compressed reading is:
$$
\text{Good is reality-constrained positive continuation.}
$$

$$
\text{Evil is destructive orientation against such continuation.}
$$

$$
\text{Beauty is finite form revealing surplus order.}
$$

$$
\text{Ugliness is finite form distorting or blocking readback.}
$$
